exposure: Cerebral bypass surgery for Moyamoya disease
Timing of cerebral revascularization relative to pregnancy (pre-bypass vs. post-bypass)
cohort: The study included 56 women with Moyamoya disease who underwent cerebral bypass surgery at Stanford Medical Center between 1990 and 2018, some of whom had pregnancies before and all had pregnancies after the surgery.
finding: Post-bypass pregnancy in women with Moyamoya disease is associated with low rates of neurological and obstetric complications, with cerebral revascularization prior to pregnancy linked to lower odds of perinatal stroke or TIA.
mod_finding: The overall rate of cesarean delivery among the study participants was 39%.
